author: Michael Larabel
description: Jemalloc 5.3.1 was released today with next month marking four years since the prior release, jemalloc 5.3.0. While the version bump may not seem like much, jemalloc 5.3.1 comes with many performance improvements, new features, and other enhancements...
title: jemalloc 5.3.1 Released With Many Improvements After Nearly Four Year Hiatus

author: Michael Larabel
description: For those that had purchased a StarBook MK VI laptop 3+ years ago over the advertised support for Coreboot, Star Labs has now delivered with a Coreboot build finally available and working for this AMD Ryzen 5000 series powered laptop...
title: Coreboot Comes To AMD Ryzen Powered Star Labs StarBook MK VI After 3+ Year Wait

author: Michael Larabel
description: On this first day of the Linux 7.1 merge window, among the early pull requests merged were beginning to land the various VFS pull requests submitted by Christian Brauner. Among that code merged is enabling support for user.* extended attributes on sockets...
title: user.* xattrs On Sockets Merged For Linux 7.1 As Sought By GNOME & systemd Developers

author: Michael Larabel
description: The Spack package manager is quite popular in the HPC / supercomputer space for scientific software. Even with the more selective niche than a typical general purpose OS package manager, large language models (LLMs) have already proven capable of being useful in generating new Spack packages. But there have also been some headaches involved too for Spack developers...
title: The Good & The Bad When Using LLMs To Write Spack Packages

author: Michael Larabel
description: In advance of the Linux 7.1 merge window opening, Miguel Ojeda sent out all of the Rust feature updates on Friday. This includes bumping the minimum Rust version for building the Linux kernel as well as a new experimental option that can provide better performance for Rust code within the kernel, alongside other updates...
title: Rust For Linux 7.1 Bringing Experimental Option That Can Help Performance

author: Michael Larabel
description: Sent out today was an initial patch series for comment on introducing the FTRFS file-system. The FTRFS proposal is more interesting than last week's VMUFAT file-system proposal...
title: FTRFS: New Fault-Tolerant File-System Proposed For Linux

author: Michael Larabel
description: Mold 2.41 is out as the latest major update to this high performance linker and viable alternative to the linkers from the GNU and LLVM projects...
title: Mold 2.41 Linker Released With New Features & Fixes

author: Michael Larabel
description: For those wishing to make use of modern OpenCL 3.0 capabilities on AMD APUs/SoCs with integrated Radeon graphics using Mesa's Rusticl driver, an improvement was merged this weekend to the RadeonSI driver ahead of this quarter's Mesa 26.1 release...
title: Mesa 26.1 RadeonSI Driver Lands Improvement For AMD APUs With Rusticl

author: Michael Larabel
description: Nearly one year ago to the day I noted Linux developers were considering the removal of the Apple HFS and HFS+ file-system drivers from the kernel. They were orphaned the past decade and turning into a maintenance burden for upstream developers. But then to some surprise, a few developers stepped up to maintain the HFS(+) drivers. One year later it's proving to be a success story with more fixes for this aging Apple file-system support continuing...
title: Apple HFS / HFS+ File-System Support Seeing Many Fixes For Linux 7.1

author: Michael Larabel
description: Among the early pull requests sent out to Linus Torvalds even before the Linux 7.0 kernel officially released on Sunday were the Btrfs file-system updates. This feature-packed CoW file-system is seeing more performance optimizations for Linux 7.1 as well as its shutdown ioctl feature no longer being experimental and a variety of fixes...
title: Btrfs Brings Performance Improvements, Shutdown ioctl Stable With Linux 7.1

author: Michael Larabel
description: Building off last night's release of the Linux 7.0 kernel is now the GNU Linux-libre 7.0-gnu kernel release for that downstream kernel that removes support for loading non-free-software kernel modules, blocks the loading of loadable microcode/firmware even when it means greatly reduced hardware support, and other sanitization of code in the name of software freedom...
title: GNU Linux-libre 7.0 Deals With Deblobbing More Drivers & Cleansing DT Files
